featured_reviews.name: Mehul Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly very disappointed with the service experience at this Achija outlet. After entering and being seated, no glasses or water were provided until we had to call someone and ask for it ourselves. The place wasn’t even crowded, which made the lack of attention even more surprising.

Throughout the visit, we had to repeatedly ask the staff for basic things — taking orders, providing glasses and water, cleaning the table, bringing the washing bowl, etc. It felt like we constantly had to remind them for everything instead of the service happening naturally. Compared to the Worli and Ghatkopar Achija outlets, the service here felt far below standard.

Food was disappointing too. The dal khichdi was quite tasteless, and we had ordered Paneer Charminar but were served Paneer Lababdar instead.

When you’re charging premium prices for food, basic service and attentiveness are the minimum expected. Otherwise, what’s really the difference between visiting a reputed restaurant and eating at a normal place?

Visited around 12:30 AM, so parking wasn’t an issue, but overall the food and service experience really didn’t match the expectations we usually have from Achija.

The overall experience was decent. It is a very good option for vegeterian food among many vegeterian restaurants in Kandivali.

featured_reviews.name: The foodie world
featured_reviews.review_text:
Achija in Kandivali East is one of those classic family restaurants that never disappoints. While it’s most famous for its pav bhaji, my visit turned out to be a complete feast with a mix of flavors. The pav bhaji with butter garlic chutney truly lived up to the hype—rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced, with that chutney taking it to another level. The paneer hotpan was sizzling and full of flavor, while the Mexican cheese roll was cheesy, crunchy, and indulgent. For South Indian cravings, the thatte idli was soft, fluffy, and really comforting.

On the drinks side, the pink guava and peach ice tea were refreshing and balanced, and the Kit Kat shake was a fun, chocolatey treat to end the meal. Achija is definitely a place where you can enjoy a wide variety of dishes under one roof, making it perfect for family outings. The vibe is casual, the food is consistently good, and the menu has something for everyone.

We ordered a variety of dishes, including multiple soups, paneer and veg starters, veg and paneer sabzis, butter rotis, and matka biryani. All the food was served promptly, and everything tasted fantastic. This is a pure veg restaurant we highly recommend to anyone looking for delicious food and a welcoming atmosphere. Perfect for family outings!

This was an Indian version of sizzler. Served with authentic vegetable pulao and creamy makhani sauce. I loved the paneer steaks which were presented in heart shape❤️. It was a blast of flavour in every bite with a mild sweetness of makhani sauce.

featured_reviews.name: Ronit Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were looking for a new restaurant to have dinner and then thought of trying this restaurant. The restaurant is actually a medium-sized one not too big but is well maintained.

Coming to the order we started by order Veg. Fingers for a starter. There were 10 pieces all crisp and hot. The schezwan chutney they served with those fingers truly improved the taste. The fingers were made from all kinds of veggies and I could see corns, carrots, and potato at least. All in all the taste was delicious.

Next, we ordered Veg. Chilly Milly, and Paneer Handi for the main course along with Butter Rotis and Butter Naan for the main course. The Veg. Chilly Milli was as its name on the spicier side with veggies such as French beans, carrots, cauliflower, etc. made in an orange gravy. While the paneer handi actually came in a handi and had nice big cubes of paneer. The paneer was soft and you could really enjoy chewing it. The paneer handi too was in an orange gravy but less spicy than the prior one. The taste and quantity of both were superb and a good thing was they also took care to ensure they do not add any capsicum as we had asked.

The butter rotis and butter naan were soft and were roasted perfectly. There were no black marks on any of them showing perfection. Also, there was a generous quantity of butter on the rotis and naan which really enriched the taste of the entire food. Finally, we ended the meal with a glass of sweet lime juice. Served slightly cold but was really soothing after a spice enriched food. All in all, we thoroughly enjoyed our dinner and I would definitely recommend trying out this restaurant.

But i must say Nirvana has taken care of  each and everything perfectly. From keeping hygiene taking temperature and proper sanitisation. featured_reviews.review_text:
This location is in Kandivali East . And it’s really a very nice restaurant . Niravana is a family dining restaurant and this place can be visited with friends and with family also . They have a great variety of cuisines which is served here from starters , main course , soups , chinese , sizzlers and even the best mocktails and desserts .
Had tried as lot of varietie of cuisines here and they are just amazing .
In the mocktail had tried the kiwi stroke - this mocktail contain green apple , kiwi and soda it’s really refreshing and amazing there are small pieces of kiwi and green apple and it’s just worth trying . One of the best mocktails which is served here .
Then had tried the litchi lemonade - this mocktails contains litchi , lemon and soda . It’s just so unique and it has litchi pieces in it and the mocktail is just amazing and this one of my favourite too.
Then had tried the desi cheese fondue - this fondue is just so cheesy and yummy and it’s served with lots of cheese and bread pieces and potatoes . This is just the best combination to have .
Pizza kulchiyaan - this started is really unique and it’s hot buttery mini kulchas stuffed with pizza stuffing which is little tangy and yummy with just so soft and temption . One the most unique dish and it’s the best ans recommended.
Then the sizzlers here are also really very nice .
Had tried the Panner manchurian sizzler - this sizzler is served with Panner pieces with rice and it’s served with chilly sauce and veggies and this really tasty and topped French fries and all the stuffs in the sizzler just combine so well.
Really love the service here as it’s really good and the staff is really very polite and nice and the food served here is fresh and the quality and the quantity of the food is really great. Surely going to visit this place .

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Shedge
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vijay is a wonderful vegetarian restaurant that truly stands out, not just for its food but for the warmth of its hospitality. The owner, a kind and attentive senior citizen, personally takes interest in every guest’s experience. It’s rare to see someone so dedicated—he actively asks for feedback and ensures that every dish meets your expectations.

What impressed me the most is his willingness to make things right immediately. If something feels off in taste, he doesn’t hesitate to have it corrected or replaced, showing genuine care for customer satisfaction. This level of attentiveness creates a welcoming and comfortable dining environment.

The food itself is fresh, flavorful, and prepared with consistency. Combined with the owner’s humble nature and openness to feedback, Vijay offers more than just a meal—it delivers a heartfelt dining experience that makes you want to come back again.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located on the Western Express Highway Jivhala Restaurant is a hidden gem.

Ambiance: It's simple, and classy. It gives the fine dine feeling with a homely touch. The decor is simple and yet I fell in love with it. The old  vessels, and the tiny figurines adorning the wall give it such a homely touch. Oh and their menu card is wood carved menu.

Service: It's quick and best part even the staff speak Marathi. To me that definitely is a +1for them.

Food:
(Note: Some of the dishes I've clicked mid way through eating 🙈 so forgive me.)

We started of with the super delicious drumstick soup. That's a must try if you visit the place.

• Kothimbir wadi: Tiny discs that don't look like Kothimbir wadi but tastes like it. Crisp, crunchy yet melt in the mouth.

• Alu wadi: Now that was tad bit disappointing. It lacked the typical Maharashtrian touch. But somehow I still liked the way it was prepared I could taste the Alu and the layer of filling.

• Sabudana wada: Picture perfect, crisp, crunchy, slightly less on salt and flavour but that's made up by the amazing chutney.

•Gavran chicken thali: One of the most delicious delicious gavran chicken thali. Super soft, beautifully cooked, mouth melting chicken. Ah, after ages I've had something so soul full. The thali consisted of the soup, chicken sukka, curry, bhakri, rice, Sol kadi. A definite must try as per me.

• Prawn thali: A thali with sukka, curry, Sol kadi, rice and bhakri.

Desserts included the seasons special gajar halwa and kharvas😍

Best part: You can customise your meals according to your taste buds

featured_reviews.name: Anushka Tol
featured_reviews.review_text:
Service- 5/5
Food Quality- 5/5
Ambience- 5/5
Must try- Misal Pav, Thal Peeth, Drumstick Soup, Pitla Bhakar, Kothambir Wadi, Gajar Halwa and other signature dishes
Jivhala offers a lot of great dishes from the Maharashtrian Cuisine. It is located near thakur complex. I tried a lot of vegetarian dishes.
Starting with Kothambir wadi, the crisp will make one fall in love with it. Sabudana wade with the chutney had a pure authentic taste. Thal Peeth was medium spicy with a special chutney served along with it. Pitla bhakar is a must-try-dish here; medium spicy, the pitla is perfect balance of ingredients and spices while the bhakar is art, soft to touch and yummy in taste. The misal pav served is very similar to the original taste back from internals of maharashtra, spicy but giving oneself cravings. Other dishes I tried includes the punjabi dish Veg Kolhapur, which has a maharashtrian taste to it and biryani.

Butter Milk and Mattha served leave their footprints on the taste buds and are crafted from perfect curd. Gajar Halwa is must-try sweet dish. It is very similar to the very own taste from home made by our mother. The Drumstick soup is very tasty.

The ambiance here is excellent. The place is huge, containing all that makes it look Maharashtrian. The lights are in perfect sync with the instrumental music. There's indoor as well as outdoor sitting available.

Authentic NON-VEG dishes is the specialty of this restaurant. Large menu is available for the same.
Overall, the quantity and quality of all the dishes here is great. A great place to have family dinner.

featured_reviews.name: coco
featured_reviews.review_text:
The comfort of shiny steel plates and a clean and simple surrounding with a touch of homely vibes surely do say it with all pride that you are in for a regional delight. Jivhala, The Maharashtrian Kitchen efficiently manages to bring to life the delight and soulfulness of typical Maharashtrian dishes and defines what it truly is to go Maharastrian. We recently visited them to get a taste of ethnic Marathi cuisine and we were thoroughly impressed.
To start with, we treated ourselves with the Limbu Sarbat as well as the Kokam Sarbat. It would not seem appropriate to try out a Maharashtrian meal without these two. The limbu sharbat was decent but the sourness could be toned down a bit. The kokam sharbat on the other hand was extremely refreshing and flavourful.
Next up was another lip-smacking favourite, the Mumbaikar's meal, the Misal Pav. This one was spicy and subtle in all the required places. The flavours blended in unison and created a wonderful and perfectly spicy blend of tastes. The lentils and the rassa were amazing together. Overall, it was really good.
Next one was the Cheese Vada Pav. Unlike the usual ones where it’s just a cheese slice over the wadas, they integrated the cheese into their stuffing. The spice of wada and the gooey cheese blended well and created a fitting of flavours and gooey-ness. Served with chutney, it was perfectly in sync with a true Mumbaikar’s taste.
Next one was a speciality, the Bhajaniche Thalipeeth. It was made up of 7 different flours and served with an amazing sweet-sour chutney. The thalipeeth had a nice texture and was crispy as well as the chutney had the zingy touch to it.
We tried yet another speciality, the Mulberry Mastani. Now, this one was something. The raw flavor of mulberries and a chilling cold creamy taste of mastani was enough to give this summer heat, a beat. The mastani is a famous drink in Pune and they are probably one of the rare ones serving it in Mumbai.
They have even given a Maharashtrian twist to the Firangi sandwich with a hint of Mumbai. The Sandwich Masala Pav was basically a stack of veggies placed between regular pav and topped with lots of masala coriander was their version of masala pav. It tasted pretty good and definitely something you would munch upon in a quick mode.
The cheese pav bhaji toast was a simple dish. Spicy pav bhaji served on a slightly toasted bread and topped with loads of cheese. This one was well put up and had a great taste too.
Next was the Shengdana Gul Podi. Unlike our usual puranpoli, it was made with a mixture of jaggery with crushed peanuts. The mixture gave it sort of a crunch and kept the texture of puranpoli intact.
The Sabudana Wada, is definitely something you wouldn't want to miss on your visit down here. Crunchy and soft, at the same time, it was served with spicy green chutney. It was delicious and had a load of bursting flavours in it.
Our meal ended with Gajar ka Halwa. Traditional and simple, this dish can win over hearts. Well, it did the same with us too. Not only was the taste perfect, but even the quantity of ghee was proper. We absolutely loved it.
The place spells home and so do their dishes. If you are looking forward to get back in touch with your Maharashtrian self then this one will be one of those places who will definitely do the job for you.

Ambience: 3.5/5
Taste Quotient: 4.5/5
Service: 5/5

Raghusiya – Kandivali | Gujarati comfort with a sweet soul

We visited Raghusiya for a proper sit-down meal, and from the very first bite it’s clear this place stays true to its Gujarati roots.
📍 Location & Access
One of the biggest wins here is the approach. It’s conveniently located near Kandivali station, on the Churchgate side, close to the East–West bridge. Easy to spot, easy to reach.
Plus, they have valet parking, which instantly removes half the stress of eating out in this part of the city.
🍽 The Food
If you enjoy sweet-leaning Gujarati flavours, you’ll feel right at home here. The food carries that familiar Gujarati touch subtle sweetness, comforting textures, and balanced spices. Nothing aggressive, nothing overpowering  just food that’s meant to be enjoyed slowly.
The dishes we tried were well-prepared, neatly presented, and clearly made with consistency in mind. This is not experimental cuisine  it’s traditional food done the way it’s meant to be.
⚡ Service
Service was quick and efficient, which really helps when the place is buzzing. Orders arrived on time, and the staff seemed well-versed with the menu and flow.
Final thoughts:
Raghusiya is a solid choice if you’re craving Gujarati-style comfort food, want easy accessibility, and don’t want to wrestle with parking woes. Sweet flavours, swift service, and a location that works in its favour.

featured_reviews.name: Prasad Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hospitality destroyed by arrogance, not service.

We visited this restaurant with a family group of ten, including two elderly parents, in-laws, women, and one little child. Despite a confirmed booking, the manager reserved sofa seating for fourteen people who never arrived. When I politely asked about this, he dismissed me saying “Aapko nahi samaj ayega.” Later, when I called him over for ordering A bhai idhar aa, he publicly warned me in front of my whole family: “Aap kerke bulao.”

Such language is not only disrespectful but can traumatize children and elders. I was not under the influence of alcohol—had anyone been drinking, this could easily have escalated into a brawl. As a regular customer, I now wonder how I can return, especially if the same staff continues to treat guests this way. In Bombay, saying “Tu” is common language, but in this restaurant a professional setting staff should be addressed respectfully as Aap—especially when they are around 38 years of age.

Maybe the guy manager was bothered by my cross-question about the booking. But if he had simply explained that the sofa was booked prior to mine, or assured me that we would be shifted if no one showed up, I would have been satisfied. If tone or disrespect was a concern, he could have asked the owner not to assign him the task of dealing with me. There were many professional ways to handle the situation, but instead he chose to insult me in front of my family.

Hospitality should be about dignity and respect. Management must take this seriously and train staff so no other family faces such humiliation in the future is my humble request to the owner of the beautiful and one of the best restaurant.

The food was outstanding. Every single dish was seasoned beautifully, plated like art and tasted even better than it looked. You can tell there is actual technique + real love in the kitchen. Portions and value also surprised me you leave satisfied and not overwhelmed.
Ambience was romantic, premium, modern, and they kept sound levels where you can actually speak normally without yelling which I appreciate so much.
If you’re looking for a place that feels special, memorable, and truly elevated go to Ebony Fine Dine. This is a restaurant that understands both hospitality and culinary craft at a high level. I will 100% be coming back and telling everyone about this place.
